text: In Physics IV.14, Aristotle raises the question of whether, since time is the number of motion and number requires a counter, time could exist at all without a ___ to count it.
explanation: Aristotle asks whether there could be time without a soul (or intellect) to do the counting: if number requires a counter and only a soul counts, then time as counted number seems to depend on soul - though he hedges that the before-and-after substrate of motion could exist without soul. The passage anticipates later debates over temporal idealism. The expected answer is 'soul.'
